title: RFK Jr. Visits the Vieques Hospital. He Brought the Scissors and the Ribbon, but They Needed a Night Shift Doctor: The Ferry Still Makes the Diagnosis and the Ventilator Hasn't Arrived.
description: In September 2026, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Governor Jenniffer González-Colón cut the ribbon on the new Susana Centeno Hospital in Vieques: $85.5 million, an FAA-certified heliport, an emergency room, dialysis and infusion centers, imaging and behavioral health, nine years after Hurricane María finished off the clinic that opened in 1996. This episode sets the official press releases next to the local briefings and reads the receipts: the years of a clinic parked in a storm shelter, dialysis patients crossing the sea three times a week, and the January 2020 death of 13-year-old Jaideliz Moreno Ventura, whose family bagged oxygen by hand because the shelter had no working ventilator; FEMA obligated $39.5 million two weeks later. Kennedy's own history on the island: 30 days in the Guaynabo federal detention center in 2001 for walking onto the Navy's bombing range. The cancer numbers that swing with every study window. And the formula the new building cannot escape: Medicare Advantage rates about 41% below the national average for the 96% of Puerto Rico's seniors who depend on them, a 4.01% increase for 2027 against a 41% gap, the 0.70 floor that Dr. Greg Murphy and 13 Republicans asked Kennedy for, and the Medicaid cliff of September 30, 2027. The heliport is an admission of failure dressed as a ribbon. The true test is the night shift.
short_title: RFK Jr. Visits the Vieques Hospital: He Brought the Scissors, but They Needed a Night Shift Doctor.
